notes.title: Version 0.70.0.0 Engine Update
notes.content:
This is updating the Godot engine to the latest version. We are doing this for ease of updating going forwards, several key fixes (text no longer tears at non-native resolution hooray!), and some minor performance gains for some hardware.

Please note that this is a VERY large upgrade in terms of under the hood changes, so please report any issues you encounter so we can address them ASAP.  Once this is confirmed all stable, its back to working on the next content update for me!

[h2]Game Engine Upgrade[/h2]
[list]
[*] Tons of under the hood changes to support the new engine version, there will be minor visual differences all over.
[*] Certain systems should see some general performance improvements.
[*] Due to the size and amount of changes required, there might be some bugs floating around, please report any ASAP.
[*] Text tearing/squishing is fixed!
[/list]
[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Synth UI screen updated and synth pin ai point upgrade removed and refunded.
[*] R1 now grants smart craft if you didn't have it.  If you did it refunds the AI points.
[*] The top resource area no longer has settings and can show 5 at once.
[*] Cores now remember which node was selected across multiple of the same core, instead of just the last one.
[*] Fleet S nodes in galaxies 4+ have less levels and give more stats per level [*] this should make for less manual re-runs.
[*] The above means you may see a jump in stats for your current galaxy depending on your S node distribution.
[*] Warp discharge achievements now give discharge speed instead of charge speed.
[*] Tether warps automatically switch when one gets maxed or you have enough Skein to max it.
[*] Splice automation now has options to prioritize quickest to rank or level.
[*] Added initial support for Turkish.
[*] A bunch of other minor changes.
[/list]
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed issue with Base resources not quite giving the stated amount.
[*] Fixed issue with Fleet UT grid buffs when fully filled out.
[*] Fixed cloud save screen to show fresh save info when you do a cloud save.
[*] Fixed splice aspect level and rank time estimates.
[/list]

notes.title: Devlog: Engine Upgrade and Next Content Patch
notes.content:
[b]Note: this is a repost since I accidently deleted it previously >.> <.<[/b]

[h1]The Engine Upgrade[/h1]
  
We've been working on upgrading to a newer version of the Godot engine (4.5) for a while now and are very close to done. This was quite a large task, but ironically we are now waiting on some fixes on the engine side before launching the update. There is no firm ETA there, but hopefully they are all wrapped up in the next couple weeks, then we can do a final set of tests before rolling the update out.  
  
There are a bunch advantages for us in upgrading the engine, but the biggest and most noticeable one for you guys (the players) will be fixing the horrible font scaling issues that causes it to break when resizing to anything other then 1600x900. This also sets the stage for a later UI rework thanks to a bunch of internal changes with how things work in the engine.  
  
Coming up next after the engine upgrade will be a content patch, this is still a good ways out and partially depends on when/how the engine upgrade patch goes.  

[h1]Fleet/Galaxy Changes[/h1]

A big topic of discussion after the last content patch was Galaxies. There are 2 issues with how they have worked out.  
  
[b]The first[/b] is how it's rather arduous to grind through the longer galaxies, _especially_ if you are optimizing.  
[b]The second[/b] is the way Fleet and main game progression interact feeling like you often are just kind of "waiting" on finishing a galaxy to reinforce. This is exacerbated by the previous issue too.  
  
To improve the first one, existing galaxies will be having the amount of levels on S nodes (ones that grant stats) significantly reduced. Likely just the 5th and 6th galaxies as those are the main issue. This will result in a couple less runs total, but importantly, far less re-optimizing of fights. Instead of 5 levels each giving 0.1 stats, there will be 2 levels each giving 0.25. As a bonus, this will also (hopefully) solve the slightly awkward occurrence of gaining 0.1 or less stats resulting in a [i]worse[/i] result on a battle next run. Oh, and the GF nodes will have the stat bonus removed and just give more Fleet Resources. This will apply to new galaxies also. But in addition, new galaxies will be smaller, as the way that all works changes post galaxy 6!  
  
At this point, nothing is changing with existing content to address the second issue listed above. Fleet progress will be a bit faster and easier to optimize, which will hopefully help alleviate it a bit still, but upcoming content will be changing how things work. It's possible more changes come to the existing Fleet content, but that will be after this next patch (which will hopefully give more insight into things).  
  
Which brings us to...  
  
[h1]Upcoming Content[/h1]
  
[b]Spoilers of course![/b]
  
First off, Galaxies will be smaller, and a couple will unlock at a time (or perhaps very close together, pending play testing). The sweet spot seems to be around the size of the 3rd or 4th galaxy. Here is a preview of one of the new galaxy layouts that is still a work in progress, but it's got the right size/idea!  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/cb49d2f357ba1401d691fb33f2a436bc9160bf1e.png[/img]
  
Additionally, Artifact upgrades are likely getting decoupled from Reinforce at some point for the next galaxies, allowing for immediate and noticeable impact on the main game as you acquire them. This has some issues that aren't fully ironed out though, so it's unclear when that will kick in (could be as far out as 150 along with some other radical changes).  
  
Outside of Fleet, the next content update will bring the next evolution of Reactor that will unlock a bit after maxing out all the Overdrives at 20. Here is a VERY early preview of that (Ignore any specific details here, it will likely all change aside from the overarching setup)  
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/ff96989b1deb5fa16d28cd0d8ae63a52f41c62b1.png[/img]

And of course, more sectors, upgrades and QoL changes will be included.  

[h1]The UI Rework[/h1]
  
Once that's all wrapped up, focus will shift to a UI rework. This is a big part of the reason for upgrading the engine, as we really didn't want to make big changes to the UI with some of the less than stellar setups in the current version (largely, themes and font sizing).  
  
Honestly, not much is concrete here yet. The goal is to spruce things up a bit and improve the general UI, tutorials, readability and just overall look a bit nicer. Things like an actual Main Menu (allowing for Save Slots among other things) and cleaner top interface (AKA, less of a button explosion up there). And well, mobile improvements too, but you guys on steam don't care much about that :P.  
  
[h1]Feedback and Suggestions[/h1]

If you've got any feedback or suggestions (especially good UI improvement ones!), feel free to either drop by the [url=https://discord.gg/usi]Discord [/url]or make a post here in the Steam forums about them. All your guys feedback has been super helpful in improving the game so far and I value it very highly.

notes.content:

	[*] Destroying a veiled enemy now sets the multiplier instead of doing the time skip

	[*] This comes out to a bit of a buff, since OD actives and other things that ignored siphoning are now effected
	[*] Various adjustments have been made to account for that a little bit

notes.title: Devlog: Galaxy Design and The Next Galaxy
notes.content:
[b]Spoilers for next content patch ahead.[/b]

When working on a Content Update, building the next Fleet Galaxy is the part that takes the longest, even not counting the time that goes into coding the new mechanics for Fleet in that galaxy. Since the next galaxy is now a good ways along (but not fully tested, tweaked and polished or even close) I figured I'd share a tiny bit of that process.

There are several things I keep in mind when designing the galaxies now beyond just balance and feel. Basically, I want "new things" in each galaxy:
[list]
[*] New "strategic" considerations on the map.
[*] New mechanics to work around in battles. 
[*] New unlocks for ships (or new ships). 
[*] New enemies.
[/list]
Before anything else, I at least vaguely figure those out. That way I know how many and how major each new thing is so I can spread them out in the galaxy properly during work on the layout.

For the layout, I sloppily build out a diagram of the galaxy with color coding and some notes.  I build things out until the next "new thing" needs to come in, at which point I move on from this part of planning, and start plopping the nodes in game and building the battles.  This is the part that takes the longest, as while im doing this, I am running battles and sections of the map over and over to make sure the scaling is correct, the resource gain is smooth and that the battles are at least somewhat interesting. Once a section is in an "OK" state, work shifts to implementing the next "new thing" if I haven't yet, test it individually, then plan out the next section and repeat.

[b]The layout[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/74818c87e90929b57f04bcc00aa29a2ad56e1cec.png[/img]

Its important to note that I'm only roughly checking things balance/feel wise at this point. Once I've got the whole thing built, testers come in and we figure out balance and such in a far more complete fashion. While testers are running things, I move on to the truckload of new non-fleet stuff that goes into a content patch.

Once things have been run by testers and balanced/tweaked etc, I know a decent range for how many runs it will take to complete, as well as expected Artifact amounts you'll have at various points, and I can plan out the artifact upgrades grid.

As a final note, since galaxies are taking so much time to do, I'd say 1/2 the time basically, and since its actually fairly daunting on my end (this is the one thing I have hard time "starting" work on, shoulda made G5 smaller T.T), after this next patch, something about galaxies will be shifting to smooth out how quickly I can get new stuff done. Not sure what yet though.

notes.title: Challenges and Unstable Transit Rework
notes.content:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/954b77eb4ca4744e2b74047e990aa0fad9948a17.png[/img]

No new end game content other than the revamped Unstable Transit.

notes.title: Major Content Update - Fleet
notes.content:
[h2]Fleet has arrived[/h2]

Finally, the next major content update is here.

Once you hit R5, you will have access to the Fleet tab, where you will work your way through several galaxies while slowly growing your fleet. You'll need to choose which additional ships to add to your fleet, and what configurations to deploy in battle, then watch it play out in an auto battle style. Progressing through galaxies earns you more and more artifacts, which can be spent on upgrades that will trigger when you Reinforce.

While the majority of the patch is for R4+ content, there are also quite a few tweaks and QoL stuff for before that.

With this patch finally out, content in general will be coming in quicker intervals (as opposed to 6+ months ><).  I hope to expand on this content fairly rapidly for at least a little while!  A loose roadmap of more major things is below these patch notes.

Oh and giveaways running again if you swing by the [url=https://discord.gg/usi]Discord[/url]

[h3]Patch Notes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Content up to sector 120
[*] New Fleet tab starts on R5
[*] New redeemable code "somuchforoctoberer"
[*] Initial Reinforces changed to be purely sector based targets
[*] Reinforce 1-4 upgrades tweaked and some new ones
[*] Some warp upgrade costs slightly reduced to speed up the Sector 74 task list
[*] Initial Overdrive charge time increased to make 85+ in R3/R4 not quite so blazing fast
[*] Temporary code good until 12-15 "iminr1orr2andyounerfedmyoverdrive" for a 6 hour time skip
[*] Lots more engine speed related upgrades to make traveling faster 
[*] 3 New AI Upgrades available (2 for new content only)
[*] Tons of minor balance tweaks, bug fixes and QoL changes
[*] Audio: New setting - Auto buy sounds
[*] Performance: New setting - disable enemy barrier shader
[*] (PC) Setting: Lock window size
[/list]

[h3]Whats Next[/h3]
Its Spacemas again real soon, so expect the Spacemas event to come back around in December (it will be largely the same as last Spacemas).  After that there will be some minor content updates while we work on some of the bigger long term things.  Those bigger things are:

[list]
[*] Upgrading the engine to Godot 4.3 - This will help performance wise and let us do a more comprehensive theme system among other niceties
[*] UI Facelift - A lot of the UI is kind of rough, [b]and outright awful on mobile[/b]. This will aim to improve the UI across the board, including things like nice interface sounds and music.
[*] Lore update - This goes with the UI Facelift for the most part, but this game is seriously lacking any real story or narrative, even for an idle game really, even just a little bit of work on this should be a large improvement
[*] 1.0 - Once all of that is done, and there has been several content patches along side it, its time for 1.0!  
[/list]

For content, expect more sectors, galaxies and changes to systems to continue.

And as always, thanks so much for playing and enjoying the game!

notes.title: Future Content Status and Info
notes.content:
[u][b]Spoilers on new content ahead![/b][/u]

[h1]Development Status[/h1]
Its been a while since there was new end game content.  Part of that is due to other things being worked on since the last content update, mainly the 75+ re-balance and mobile version launch.  But the other reason its taking so long is just how much work there was to do to get the next major system in place.

As has been hinted/mentioned before, that new system is Fleet.  This is the final major system that was "planned" for the game and as such is the biggest and most involved.  This also means I want it to be very, very good.  And part of making it that good involves letting go of ideas that didn't work out fully or just were not good enough, so I've discarded a lot of ideas and work on it over the last several months.

[u]But as of this post, Fleet as a system is 95% in place and testing is in progress.[/u]

However, Fleet is not the [i]only[/i] thing coming in the next content patch, and there is still a bit of work to do there.  Sorry but no ETA as i'll probably just miss it

[h1]Fleet[/h1]
[u]Note[/u]: Everything in here is still subject to change and the UI is not fully done.

The core mechanic within Fleet are the Fleet Battles.  This is completely separate from the endless battling your ship does.  

[b]Instead, you will be strategically building and deploying your fleet in various battles that will then play out.[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/d292b7ed341f2e4b909afd539af19def36081166.png[/img]

[b]These battles reside within galaxies where you will increase your fleet size and capability over time.[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/cd25190e1015cb9a39c2b53fa62d3791f387605c.png[/img]

[b]Fleet ties back into the rest of the game via Reinforces in 2 ways.[/b]

First, the main way you progress in galaxies is by using Fleet Resources (name might change) to deploy your ships and make various improvements on different nodes in the galaxy.  These Fleet Resources are based on the highest sector you have Reinforced at (essentially what is currently Fleet Power in game now).  You can improve your total within a galaxy, but the more you have to begin with, the faster you can make progress.

Second, within the galaxy you will be collecting an Artifact resource, which can then be used to acquire various upgrades for other systems.  These upgrades will activate upon Reinforce.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/72816c9bcc73553bca67c9b13386fa0e8a40c492.png[/img]

To go with this, Reinforces after the 5th one will switch from the current "reach a specific sector for upgrades" style to an open ended one.

[h3]But this is an Idle game, not an Autobattler Roguelike![/h3]
Yes, this is an Idle game about managing various systems and decision making first and foremost.  What that means is the Fleet battles themselves, and the decisions around them (ship placement, which ships to bring, which upgrades to use) need to be very well balanced to be interesting and fun with some decisions to make, but not be insanely complex or bothersome to do repeatedly.

That is what I am currently working on right now and testing.  Since it is incredibly important to get right, it will probably take a while still just in that respect.

[h1]All The Rest[/h1]
In addition to Fleet coming in this next update, all the other systems will of course get more content and changes, so heres a few more minor teasers in that regard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/df8b7478a6d9276cef26dc0050c08bfd5a748ee0.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44368219/0fa1988721cf4e3da653518ff898e5b532458978.png[/img]
(No that is not the optimal setup lol)

Again, no ETA, but it is indeed closing in!

[h1]The Even Further Future[/h1]
Once this next content update is in place, future ones will come much faster (for real this time) since nothing nearly as big and development time consuming as Fleet is on the horizon.

Fleet is the final major system, but I have a lot of content planned for it and all the other systems still, so there is a ways to go!  And there are things outside of just content that are planned also.

[b]There will be quite a bit more gameplay content yet to come[/b]

[h3]Engine Upgrade[/h3]
This game is made in Godot on version 3.5.  An update to the latest version (4.3) with a different rendering engine and other improvements will be coming.  This should help performance across the board and even more noticeably on Mobile.

[h3]UI Glam Up[/h3]
The UI is still rather rough and barebones, it will be getting both a facelift in terms of looks, but also a bit of a re-arrangement in some cases.  This will also include interface sounds and more background music.

[h3]Story[/h3]
For story, all we really have is that opening text blob, and some sorta kinda storyish things in the tutorials.  I originally wanted more, but have just kept sidelining it for gameplay.  However, I do think the game would be [b]much[/b] better if there was an interesting story being revealed over time.

[h2]Thank You[/h2]
Thanks for reading, and thanks for playing.  Just developing the game has been a lot of fun, but you guys in the community have made this even better, so thanks a ton! 

Also, monthly giveaways in the [url=https://discord.gg/USI]Discord[/url] are back on track, so be sure to swing by!

notes.title: The 75-90 Rebalance
notes.content:
Spoilers for 75+

One of the things I strive for in the design of USI is a feeling of consistent progression with plenty of player agency in terms of systems to focus or decisions to make.  Unfortunately, the 75-90 section of the game largely fails at this in one way or another.  So its getting some changes!

You might recall a survey I posted here a while back about it.  That, combined with talking to people about it a ton on forums and discord has helped shape these upcoming changes.  Everything is not finished and tested but the general ideas are fairly locked in.  So here is a high level overview of whats coming to improve things.

[h3]Compute and Fighters[/h3]
Compute was meant to be the [b]main[/b] source of powering up your fighters.  This ended up not being remotely the case and Compute really, really sucks
[list]
[*] The Damage and Durability upgrades are changing to be multiplicative so that even after 20+ levels in them the next level is still noticeable
[*] A new specialization system based on total tiers gained (that run) to give a better feeling of control and "counter play" for specific enemy capital types
[/list]
[h3]Resources and Synth[/h3]
A huge bottleneck right out of the gate is the restrictively costly synth recipes, that also want the same resources as your core upgrades.  
[list]
[*] There will be a pretty significant boost to resource gain right out of the gate with the compute/fighter changes
[*] The recipe levels that reduce the capital resource cost are getting moved way up, so you will achieve 0 cost much, much sooner.
[/list]
[h3]Lack of Player Agency[/h3]
There is a purposeful lack of capital focused upgrades right when you get to 75, but the dearth of options lasts too long.  Prestige is also quite painful and restrictive making it harder to change things.  This results in low interaction opportunity and  railroading you into doing specific things too much.
[list]
[*] Again, the compute/fighter changes will help here with part of the new system
[*] A new, very minor addition to the core page at 77 that will allow for some tweaking
[*] Changes to prestige to make it less punishing and restrictive (this is not fully fleshed out yet)
[*] Scaling will be tweaked so that you don't hit 80, 85 and 90 for the reinforce targets quite so much by the skin of your teeth.  This translates into having to play less "perfectly" at certain sections
[/list]
This is not a final/complete list or anything, tons of minor tweaks are going in to fix the points above and just make things [i]feel [/i]better.

These changes are entering testing soon and should hopefully go live in May.  Of course, feel free to post more feedback/thoughts here or in the discord as I am still looking for all the feedback I can get on this section of the game.

[h1]Future Content[/h1]

Once the above is all wrapped up, its on to developing the new content.  100 is a big milestone and the new content will include the new, very large [b]Fleet[/b] system.  Its super early in actual development (really just rough prototyping and things bouncing around in my head) but its gonna be the biggest and most involved singular system so far.

And of course, new stuff for everything else too!  It is a very large update though so its quite far out :*(.  

I will do another post like this sometime down the road with more details and some actual teasers once it is further along.

notes.title: Content Patch Delayed
notes.content:
In the previous post I said a patch would hit in October even if it wasn't with all the stuff I had planned.  However, I think it's going to be better to just give it the extra couple weeks It will take to get everything in to give you guys a LOT of content.

One might think I could just put this out now, and then keep working on the last of this content and get another patch out in a couple weeks with the rest.  But from past experience with these content updates I know that once its out I will be endlessly distracted for at least a month with requested feature implementations, bug fixes, and other small things.  Which would mean I would not get back to getting this content in for a while.

I will post some teasers when I get a concrete release date set, the concrete release date will come when all the content I want is in and its down to testing and polish.

Sorry for the delay and thanks for your patience!
